messages:
sara chen: Quick heads-up — PR #6732 (allocator refactor) landed in canary and I'm seeing a reproducible throughput drop on long-seq workloads (~12% P50 throughput, tail unaffected-ish). Can someone from runtime take a quick look? I attached the microbench output and a short profiler snippet. :eyes:

mike brown: Thanks for the ping. Do you have the exact commit + canary ID? I can run the same benches locally.

sara chen: Canary: canary-2026-03-16-22, commit: 9f3b7a4. Bench command ran: `./bench --suite longseq --concurrency 16 --seq-len 4096 --model llama-13b`. Summary: baseline 1100 reqs/s -> canary 970 reqs/s. Memory is slightly noisier (peak +80MB on average).

aj patel: Oof. Not huge but definitely outside expected noise. Does the PR touch the slab allocator or GC paths?

sara chen: It changes the per-request arena cleanup timing and introduces a short-lived freelist consolidation pass after every N requests (N=32 by default). The intent was to reduce fragmentation but maybe it's causing churn.

luis garcia: Can you paste the flamegraph snippet? Also curious if KV cache interactions amplify it for very long key/value caching.

sara chen: Flamegraph (top 6 frames):
```
- runtime::request::process
  - runtime::alloc::consolidate_free_list
    - runtime::alloc::mark_sweep_hint
    - runtime::kernels::attention::compute
```
The consolidate step spikes during steady-state and correlates with the throughput dip.

mike brown: CI / perf bot posted something?

ci-bot: CI: perf-check/longseq — FAILED. Regression detected: throughput delta -11.8% (p<0.01). Artifact: gs://redwood-perf/canary/2063456789/bench.log

tara nguyen: Is it possible to gate the consolidation behind an adaptive heuristic? For now, can we make N much larger to reduce frequency while we investigate?

aj patel: Makes sense. Quick mitigation: flip the flag to N=1024 and re-run canary to see if throughput recovers. If it does, we know frequency is the issue.

sara chen: I pushed a patch `pr-6732-hotfix` with N=1024 and kicked off a canary. Patch: `git diff --prune ...` (short link: https://git.internal/r/6732/hotfix).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy canary-2026-03-17-01 started for pr-6732-hotfix.

mike brown: I'll re-run the local bench against the hotfix branch later today. If the canary shows improvement we can fast-track a rollback or merge hotfix.

luis garcia: Also request to add a small unit test that simulates repeated tiny allocations to ensure we don't regress again. I can take that if someone splits it out.

sara chen: Thanks — assigning test to luis. For reviewers: @mike brown @aj patel @tara nguyen — can we get approvals on either the hotfix or a revert? I don't want this staying in prod canary for long. :pray:

aj patel: Will review the hotfix now. If it fixes perf and tests are green, I'm ok approving and merging.

mike brown: Saw the hotfix canary numbers — throughput back to 1085 reqs/s (within noise). Looks good to me.

ci-bot: Canary report for pr-6732-hotfix: throughput delta -1.4% (not significant). All perf checks: PASS.

tara nguyen: Approved the hotfix PR, leaving a comment to follow up on an adaptive heuristic design in a separate issue.

sara chen: Thanks all. I'll merge the hotfix and open an RFC issue to rework the consolidation strategy (link: https://git.internal/issues/RED-1254). I'll also attach the bench artifacts and the flamegraph to the issue.

mike brown: Nice triage. Recommend we add a perf guard (SLO alert) specifically for allocator churn during long-seq runs so this shows up in the perf regression checks earlier.

luis garcia: Agree. I'll add a small synthetic microbench to the perf suite that targets this pattern.

sara chen: Closing loop — merged hotfix at commit d4c2b7e, canary promoted. Will follow up with the RFC and test PR. Thanks for the quick responses. :tada:
